page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 machine family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tier for compute-heavy workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show read-only small block cached speeds at 161.16 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 20.93 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, software compilation, image processing, and text processing benchmarks demonstrate weak to poor performance profiles.

Despite lower raw compute and memory throughput, the instance maintains average performance for specific tasks, such as text generation using a small 135M LLM model, which achieves 104.71 tokens per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 4.19 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations perform at 4.02 million operations per second. This profile suggests a cost-efficient resource density for workloads that do not require high-frequency processing or intensive memory bandwidth. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight application hosting.
